fc.x: Fractal Audio's FC-6 and FC-12 foot controllers let you control the Axe-Fx III, FM9 and FM3. The FM3 and FM9 support two FCs, the Axe-Fx III supports four FCs.
The FC controllers can not be used with the VP4 and AM4.
The FC controller and the software editor are both clients to the processors. Switching on one client will automatically update all other connected clients and the Axe-Fx III, FM3 or FM9 itself.
The FC-6 is the same size as an FM3. The FC-12 is the same size as an FM9. The only difference between the FC-6 and FC-12 is the number of available switches.

i: The entire product line was conceived years ago. The goal was to maximize the number of parts shared between products. The footswitch PC boards do three switches each. An FM3 has one board. An FC6 has two. An FM9 has three and an FC12 has four. All products use the same LCDs, encoders, side plates, etc., etc. This reduces cost and repair inventory. The FC6 and the FM3 are basically the same enclosure. The FC12 and FM9 are basically the same enclosure. This isn't a huge market. Margins are thin so you have to think of ways to minimize development and product costs. Parts bin methodology is the route we took on this generation. You can hook an FC-6/12 to it. So for small gigs/rehearsals use the FM-3 alone. For larger gigs connect an FC (or two).

If anyone is curious the thought process was this: FM3 alone for rehearsals, small gigs. FM3 plus FC6/12 for larger gigs. Axe-Fx III plus FC6/12 for MSG. (Madison Square Garden) Since the FC6/12 are "thin clients" you can exchange them with the Axe-Fx III and FM3 without having to do any programming.

All the displays are transflective so they don't wash out under bright light.
The LCDs are transflective, meaning they are visible in complete darkness to full, direct sunlight.

fc.x: The LED rings are different colors based on function. The intensity (brightness) of the switch rings can be set in the configuration.

i: The switches aren't conventional switches. They are capacitive sense switches. If you hold down a switch during boot you mess up the calibration routine. Don't do that.
Fractal Audio products use capacitive sensors instead of switches. This means they're ultra-quiet and never wear out.

fc.x: The firmware for the Axe-Fx, III, FM and FM9 also covers the FC controllers. See Firmware .

For low level functions, the FC controllers rely on separate dedicated internal firmware. Updating this is only required when Fractal Audio says so. Watch the FC's main display during startup to see its current internal firmware version. The Mark I and Mark II series have different low level firmware.
FASLINK is the bidirectional communications protocol that links the Axe-Fx III, FM9 and FM3 to FC controllers, using a single XLR (microphone) cable. Read FASLINK for more information.
FC controllers can't be used with the Axe-Fx II, AX8, FX8. The FC controllers do not support FASLINK version 1, MIDI or Ethernet/EtherCON.
The FC controllers don't have MIDI ports and can't be used by themselves to control MIDI devices directly.

However, the connected processors have MIDI OUT ports. The FC controller can initiate MIDI operations through Control switches , which are transmitted via the MIDI OUT port on the processor, or via the Scene MIDI block .

i: The system has a MIDI jack. It's on the Axe-Fx III! Actions on the foot controller can cause MIDI to be transmitted to downstream devices.

fc.x: The USB port on FC controllers is not in use, currently.

i: Future expansion. Currently it does nothing but in the future we may enable it so it can be a "USB MIDI Controller".

fc.x: You can connect up to 4 expression pedals with TRS cables. You can assign functions to these pedals, separately from the expression pedal ports on the Axe-Fx III, FM9 or FM3. Calibration and configuration of the pedals is done through the FC Controllers menu in SETUP.
See the Pedals and switches tab.

i: […] The expression pedal inputs on the Axe-Fx and on the FC6/12 have pullup resistors. If a pedal is unplugged the value goes to 100%. This is done so that if a pedal is connected to volume and you forget your volume pedal you'll still have sound.

fc.x: You can connect up to 4 external switches. Use a TS cable for a single switch (all devices), and TRS for dual switches. Configuration is done through the FC Controllers menu in SETUP.
See the Pedals and switches tab.

i: STAND IN SWITCHES - This feature broadens the capabilities of external footswitches on the FC-6 or FC-12. An external switch can operate globally as a “remote control” for any switch in any FC layout. For example, imagine an FC where Layout 6/Switch 1 has been set to "BANK +1" (tap) and "BANK -1" (hold). When we assign an FC External Switch as a stand-in for Layout 6/Switch 1, that external switch performs the bank up/down functions, even when Layout 6 is not loaded on the FC. The stand-in is an exact surrogate for the onboard switch, and can even be used with per-preset functions. Find the “Stand-In Switches” page in the “FC Controllers” menu under SETUP. NOTE: Momentary switches will probably be preferred for use as stand-ins, because they more closely mimic the behavior of the on-board switches. Note: Stand-in switches only work with external switches, not the expression pedals…

fc.x: Go to FC controllers in the Setup menu, or use FC-Edit and FC Per-Preset in the editor.
The Per-Preset configuration menu on the Axe-Fx III, FM9 and FM3 is reached via the Controllers menu.
Note that some parameters may be available on the hardware only.

i: All configuration data is stored in the Axe-Fx III. There is no management software needed for the FC. Configuration is done via the Axe-Fx III (or Axe-Edit).

fc.x: Executing Reset hardware on the Axe-Fx III, FM9 or FM3 will also reset the FC's configuration.
Restore a backup, created with the editor or with Fractal-Bot, or restore the default layout using the FC Controllers menu in SETUP or the editor.
Use Fractal-Bot to back up and restore the settings of the FC controller(s).
Use FC-Edit in the editor to back up and restore FC layouts.
You can configure whether preset names and scenes are should be preceded by a number in the main display or not.
The parameter 'Main-LCD Display Mode' lets you decide how to display songs, setlists, presets and scenes titles.
When set to 'Automatic', the display depends on the switch configuration. When songs and setlist aren't being used, the preset title appears on the first line, and the scene title on the 2nd line.
You can increase visibility by enabling the “Mini-LCD Invert Mode” option.

Normally, the FC-6 shows the first six switches in two rows, but the FC-12 places these across one row, on the bottom. Therefore, if you create a layout for the FC-12, it will re- arrange itself when viewed on an FC-6, which can be a bit confusing. To prevent this from happening, you can enable "FC-6/FC-12 Compatibility Mode".
EZ Mode lets you tap a switch and then configure its Tap and its Hold functions. Use other tab pages in this menu for advanced configuration, copying and more.
Things you can assign to switches:

i: Presets (make sure to also set Bank Size to the correct value)
Banks
Scenes
Effects (engage or bypass)
Channels
Tuner
Tempo and Metronome

Control Switches

fc.x: The FC will sometimes briefly display messages, for example when turning an effect on and off. In the FC configuration you specify the on-display time for these messages.
Tip: an edited preset can be saved during a performance through a foot switch. Assign the function Amp Level+Save with a value of 0 dB.
Switches on the FC controllers can act as Control switches . Use these to transmit MIDI, or control modifiable parameters.

The FC configuration allows allow adding each of the six Control Switches to a mutually exclusive group. Any switch with Exclusivity enabled becomes a member of a group in which only ONE switch can be turned on at once. Turning any switch in the group ON will turn all others in the group OFF automatically.
The switches support two types of action: Tap and Hold.
To engage the Hold function, tap-and-hold the switch.

In the FC's configuration you can set HOLD to either Automatic or Switch Up. Automatic means that the Hold function will kick in after a specified period (default 0.5 sec). The time that a switch has to be held for the Hold function to kick in, can be set. Switch Up means that Hold will kick in after releasing the switch.

The Hold function of a switch is not indicated on the mini display. It's briefly displayed when executing the TAP function. To see the hold function of a switch, assign a switch to Reveal Hold. There's no visual clue when activating the HOLD function.

Important: for the fastest response time from a switch, do not assign a hold function. Switches with a hold function assigned to them fire on switch release, not on switch press. If you need the switch to fire on press, remove the hold function on the switch.

Smart Bypass allows Channel switches to serve double duty by engaging or bypassing an effect. To use this option, stomp again on the footswitch for a currently selected channel. This allows you to set up separate switches for different channels without the need for a separate “Bypass” Switch.

The FC controllers provide eight layouts. Similar to pages and layers on other controllers, layouts re-map the physical switches (6 on the FC-6, 12 on the FC-12), allowing the use of the available switches for multiple tasks.
Switch to a different layout by pressing an assigned layout switch in the current layout or by using the Master Layout Menu (MLM).

Layout Linking is a feature that allows any footswitch to also change layouts. For example, if a switch is assigned to recall a preset, it can also switch to the programmed Scenes layout. Layout-Links are the trick behind the FM3's OMG9 factory layout.
To load the factory default layout(s), use the FC Controllers menu under SETUP.
The documentation provides a number of layout examples.

i: The FC series are like 12 foot controllers in one. The FC foot controllers feature 12 "layouts". Each layout has a unique, user-assignable set of switch functions. For example Layout 1 could have five preset switches, five scene switches and two switches assigned to bank up/down. Press and hold the bottom right switch and the then tap the switch above it and you enter Layout Select mode. Then tap a switch to select a new Layout. This new layout could have six channel switches and six bypass switches. Etc.

[…] You can actually assign a button to Layout so you can get there with a tap. You can also assign a button to bring up a specific layout so you could have two layouts each with a button that switches to the other layout. And the way the Layout press-and-hold works is that you press one button and while holding it tap the button above. IOW, you press the bottom button with your heal and then tap the button above. Each tap (while holding the bottom button) brings up a new layout.

fc.x: You can download blank layout templates for the FC-6 and F-12 in .pdf, .jpg formats, and as Google Sheets .

The FM3 has three onboard switches and can't show all twelve switches in a layout, which applies to the FM9 too. Therefore it provides the (Layout) Views feature. This lets you you shift the focus within a layout, like a window.
This is explained in the Owner's Manual .

The Master Layout Menu (MLM) shows all layouts on a single page (FC-12) or two pages (FC-6). Recall the MLM by holding the bottom right switch and tapping the switch above it (this can be disabled in the configuration). The FC-6 can display only six layouts at a time, so press the MLM combo switch a second time to reach the remaining layouts. So even, if you forgot to program other layout switches on your current layout, you can still get out of the current layout by engaging the MLM.
You can also assign the MLM switch to any tap or hold switch.
Notes:

i: If the lower right switch has a Tap function, it will not be activated by the MLM Switch Combo
If the lower right switch has a Hold function, you can still easily execute the MLM Switch before the Hold function kicks in

fc.x: The MLM Switch Combo can be disabled in the settings.
On the FM3, the MLM is normally assigned to the Hold function of the middle switch.
The layouts (described above) are global, meaning that they apply to all presets.
If you need preset-specific switches, you can program these in the Controllers > Per-Preset menu. This menu allows you to override global layout switches.
Per-Preset Switch Overrides can be disabled globally.

OMG refers to a set of foot switch layouts for the FM3 when used with a single FC-6 ( OMG9 ) or FC-12 ( OMG15 ). It can be installed through Setup > FC Controllers on the Axe-Fx or through Setup > FC Controllers/Onboard Switches > Reset menu on the FM3.
See the OMG User Guides for more information.

OMG3 is a variant, created by forum member Patzag, for the FM3 without the FC-6. It is available for download in the forum. OMG3 can be used with an FC-6, effectively making it act as OMG9 by following the instructions in Patzag's update .
A modified version of OMG9 allows quick access to songs and sections. Download it here
The FM9 has its own custom layouts.

i: Added new Setlists/Songs feature, which can be used with an FC Controller to access presets and scenes in custom order during live performance. A new Setup menu area provides full access from the front panel, with a corresponding new area of Axe-Edit which offering import/export and more. For additional details, please see the Setlists & Songs Mini-Manual, located at: Setlists & Songs Mini-Manual

fc.x: From the Mini-Manual:

i: In the world of musical performance, a “setlist” is a list of songs to be performed in order. A setlist structures a show, letting you plan ahead how to start strong, avoid lulls, and finish memorably. Setlists also help band members and crew/techs prepare, minimizing the need for questions or on-the-fly adjustments. A short singer/songwriter setlist might contain 4 songs, while a typical modern rock/pop concert setlist could range from 12 to 25 entries. A working cover band might play multiple sets covering a hundred songs or more in one night. The Fractal Audio Setlist/Song feature allows you to create an organized setlist comprised of named songs, with each song containing up to six distinct sections (e.g., intro, verse, solo, etc.). By using FC footswitches, you can easily navigate in order through the various sounds required. Song footswitches enable you to select songs, while…

fc.x: Songs consist of links to one or more presets and scenes. Each song can have six links/sections and can be organized into setlists. FC footswitches can change songs in order and present the various scenes needed for named song sections, intro , verse , solo , etc.. Setlists and Songs can be edited through the modeler's front panel or in the editor, which also includes utilities to import, export and more.

The Setlist & Songs feature requires an FC-6 or FC-12 Foot Controller. Designated song footswitches allow you to select songs. Section footswitches load sections from the current song. Setlist footswitches allow you to choose different Setlists. This is done in Setup > Global > FC Setlists/Songs.

Each song has a number, an up-to ten character name and contains six numbered sections. Each section has a number, an up-to ten character name, and a designation of one preset and one scene, 1-8 or DEFAULT. Up to 128 songs can be created in total.
Three SONG functions load Songs based on their numbered positions within the active setlist:

i: SELECT IN SET
Loads a song by its numbered position (1–32) in the active setlist.
TOGGLE IN SET
Toggles between two songs by their numbered positions in the active setlist.
INC/DEC IN SET

Incrementally steps forward or backward through all of the non-empty songs in the active setlist. Empty songs are skipped automatically, and any empty songs at the beginning or end of the list are skipped when the list wraps .

fc.x: Three SECTION functions load sections from the current song. Whenever a section is loaded, the main display of the FC changes to show the name of the current song, and the name of the current section. Three functions select songs from within the current active setlist:

i: SELECT
Loads a section by its number in the current song.
TOGGLE
Toggles between two Sections of the current song.
INC/DEC

Incrementally steps forward or backward through all of the sections in the current song. Empty sections are skipped automatically, and any empty sections at the beginning or end of the list are skipped when the list wraps .

fc.x: Each of the four setlists contains up to 32 songs in numbered positions. A particular song can appear more than once in the list. Empty slots are permitted only at the end. Each setlist has a number and a 10 character name. Three SETLIST functions change the active setlist:

i: SELECT
Makes the designated Setlist active by its number, 1–4.
TOGGLE
Toggles between two setlists, making them active .
INC/DEC.
Incrementally steps through the setlists to select one as active.

fc.x: Sample layouts are available at: Downloads . Descriptions are in the Mini Manual.

setup.x: In current firmware, preset, scene and channel changes are gapless, if desired. The global Gapless parameter allows turning this on or off.
The default is ON. Turn it OFF to decrease CPU usage a little.
To enable gapless preset switching on the FM9 and FM3, you also need to set Spillover to ALL and save all presets under the current firmware.

i: There are caveats: If presets are using a lot of CPU then the gapless switching may not work as there is not enough CPU available. If presets are "stale" (saved under an older revision) then gapless switching may not work until the presets are saved. This is because the preset is being updated during the switchover. If you switch presets rapidly you may get a gap because a lot of stuff goes on in the background after switching presets to get ready for the next preset change. If you switch before these background tasks are completed then you'll get a gap. It can take a few seconds for the tasks to complete.
Full-Res (room) IRs are large and take a long time to load. Gapless switching is not supported when using Full-Res IRs.

setup.x: OLDER FIRMWARE Any device that features flexible routing you have to mute, switch then unmute. This takes time. The reason is that if you don't do this then you'll end up with sound from one of the blocks that may have moved to a different position possible causing a loud pop or other artifact. For example, if you have a simple amp->cab->delay preset then you switch to a preset that has delay->amp->cab the sound from the delay will get amplified during the switch so you have to mute everything, wait for the signals to decay, rearrange the blocks, then unmute. Products with a fixed routing can switch faster since they don't have to worry about rearranging blocks. The Axe-Fx amp modeling is also far more intricate and complex than other products and this requires muting the amp modeling for a short time to allow the bias points to settle. Our modeling is very detailed and whenever the amp…
There's a global mix parameter in SETUP for reverb: Reverb Mix.
The parameter simply multiplies the Mix value in the presets.
Note that reverbs also are effected by the Effects Mix parameter (see above).

i: Global Reverb and Effects Mix are relative. If set to 0% the mix is set by the preset. If set to, say, -10% the mix would be 10% less than the preset mix.

setup.x: The Effects Mix parameter in SETUP lets you control the overall wetness of effect blocks that have a Global Mix parameter.
The parameter simply multiplies the Mix value in the presets.

i: Axe-Fx II, Axe-Fx III, AX8, FX8, FM9, FM3, VP4

setup.x: Values: Stereo, Left Only, Right Only, Sum L+R, Mono (VP4 only).

When connecting a guitar to the front instrument input on the Axe-Fx II, set this parameter to LEFT ONLY (default). You'd only use SUM L+R or STEREO when connecting a stereo instrument to Input 1 (rear). Input 1 front on the Axe-Fx III is always mono.
IMPORTANT: Do not select SUM L+R or STEREO when using only the Left input. This may introduce noise from the disconnected Right input and attenuates the signal level by 6 dB.
Input 2 Mode controls the same thing for Input 2 on the FM3, Axe-Fx II, AX8, and FX8. Input 3 Mode and Input 4 Mode control the same thing for inputs 3 and 4 on the Axe-Fx III.
There's no Mode parameter for Input 1 on the Axe-Fx III.

When using the VP4 with a single input, set Input Mode to MONO and connect to the L/Mono input only. When using the VP4 as a stereo device, make sure to set Input Mode to STEREO and always connect cables to both the left and right inputs (L/Mono and Right). The Input Mode setting is overridden when the global 4CM Routing option is enabled.

i: Axe-Fx II, Axe-Fx III, FM9, FM3, AX8, FX8, VP4, AM4

setup.x: This determines if the output signal is stereo, or one of the two mono modes: Sum L+R or Copy L>R.
From the Axe-Fx III Owner's Manual :

i: Stereo
No special settings required
Half-Stereo

Leaving the Axe‐Fx III in its default stereo conguration but connecting only one (Left) output results in a “half‐stereo” setup. This works fine, aside from the exceptions such as ping-pong, panning, etc). No special settings required
Dual Mono

Sonically, this is identical to half-stereo, with the same limitations, except that mono signal is produced at both the left and right jacks so you can connect to two monitors. To switch to dual mono, go to Setup > I/O > Audio and set Mode for the desired output to COPY L->R
Summed Mono

Left and right channels are added together resulting in an identical mono signal at both left and right outputs. This has the advantage of not discarding half of the sound, but summing has its own issues. For example, short delays or phase differences between channels can result in strange artifacts or even total cancellation. To switch to summed mono, Setup > I/O > Audio and set Output Mode for the desired output to SUM L+R

setup.x: On the VP4, USB and SPDIF audio go directly to the converters in stereo, so the Output Mode setting does not apply. Also, the setting does not apply when running the VP4 in 4CM mode.
The MUTE option in current firmware allows muting the analog outputs while still passing data via USB. This can be used in conjunction with computer plugins.

Incoming computer audio such as YouTube is NOT muted when using the MUTE OUT1 option in Setup > I/O > Audio. When recording or playing back in a DAW, with the DAW track set to USB channels 1-2, incoming audio from the DAW is also NOT muted when using the new MUTE OUT1 option, so you'll hear software monitoring only.
For more information read:

i: Mono versus stereo audio
Audio I/O and amplification
Axe-Fx III, FM9, FM3, AX8, FX8

setup.x: Set to -10dB when connecting the input to a pedal, a guitar amplifier input, or when the output is clipping the input section of another device.
Set to +4dB when connecting to the output of a pro-level device or to a louder output signal.
Note: The III and FM3 default to -10 dB nominal output level, so their output level is lower than that of the II and the AX8.
See Levels .

i: Axe-Fx III: The default Output Level for Output 1 and 2 is -10 dBv. This was done to reduce the number of support cases due to people overloading the inputs on consumer-grade interfaces, mixers, etc. (IOW cheap stuff). Most professional gear runs at +4 dBu so if using a pro-grade interface, mixer, etc. you may want to go into the Global menu and change the level to +4 dBu.

FX8: The POST LEVEL parameter switches the FX8 between +4dB (default) and -10dB. Use +4dB if the unit connects to a line-level port on another device. Use -10dB if the unit connects to a guitar amplifier's instrument input or a pedal. If you're using the FX8 in a Four Cable Method (4CM) setup, and you're experiencing hiss, try switching to another Post Level value.
Axe-Fx II, Axe-Fx III, FM9, FM3, AX8, VP4, AM4

setup.x: This lets you invert the phase of the signal, if necessary. This can be useful to reduce feedback from an acoustic guitar, control musical feedback, or improve tone.

i: Axe-Fx II, AX8, Axe-Fx III (OUT 3/4), FM9 (OUT 3), FM3 (OUT 2)

setup.x: The Boost/Pad parameter optimizes the signal level to reduce noise in certain scenarios, such as a 4CM setup (Four Cable Method), when placing the device in front of a traditional amp, or when integrating an external pedal.
The Output Boost/Pad is supported for unity gain outputs.
When putting the Axe-Fx II or III in front of a real amp using Output 3 or 4 (FM9: output 3, FM3: output 2), maximize Boost/Pad to make sure the full range of the D/A converter is used.
When using a 4CM setup: increase Boost/Pad and prevent clipping. Turn OUT LEVEL on the front panel fully open for unity gain. Use Input Level IN to finetune the signal level.
Boost/Pad is not intended for boosting USB output (although it does have that effect).

Boost/pad only applies to the outputs, that's why it's under the Output header. PREVIOUS GENERATIONS Usually you will use this when you send the effect loop out before the amp block. The signal will be weak going to the D/A converters. This allows you to boost the signal to the D/A converters w/ maintaining the same output level.

i: Axe-Fx II, Axe-Fx III, FM9, FM3, AX8

setup.x: This determines the signal that is sent from Output 2.
Axe-Fx III : ON — A copy of the Output 1 signal (excluding incoming USB audio) is sent to Output 2. OFF — The Output 2 block controls the output.

FM3 : Input 1 — Sends an exact copy of the direct input signal (unprocessed DI signal) through Output 2. Output 1 — A copy of the Output 1 signal (excluding incoming USB audio) is sent to Output 2. OFF
If the Axe-Fx III or FM3 preset contains an Output 2 block, this parameter is ignored.

Axe-Fx II : OFF Output 1 — Output 2 sends an exact copy of the Output 1 signal (excluding incoming USB audio), UNLESS the preset contains an FX Loop block. Input 1 — Output 2 sends an exact copy of the direct input signal (unprocessed). This sends a DI signal through Output 2, UNLESS the preset contains an FX Loop block.

i: Axe-Fx III, FM9

setup.x: This determines whether a copy of Output 1 is sent through Output 3 or 4, for example for reamping. It's the same as connecting the Input 1 block to the Output 3/4 block.
If the preset contains an Output 3 block or Output 4 block, this parameter is ignored.

i: FM3

setup.x: This lets you choose between LINE LEVEL and UNITY GAIN output for Output 2.

UNITY GAIN To use FM3 Out 2 in unity gain applications, such as when connecting to a tube amp or certain pedals, confirm the following settings in the Output 2 Configuration section under SETUP > I/O > Audio:

i: Output Type: Unity Gain

Boost/Pad: This optional setting may be increased to lower the noise floor. This can be useful, for example, when connecting to a "gainy" tube amp. Be careful however, as higher settings can cause clipping in the FM3. Watch the Status LEDs and reduce preset levels or turn this setting down if needed.

Output 2 Copy: Typically, None, but there are also applications for copying Input 1 to OUT 2, such as when recording an analog DI at unity gain via Out 2 while also recording the processed signal via Out 1. Remember though that placing an OUT2 block on the grid will override any Output 2 Copy setting, passing instead whatever audio is sent to the block. Other settings such as Level, Boost/Pad,…
Set Out 2 Mode and Phase as desired.

setup.x: For Unity Gain applications, set the Out 2 top panel knob fully clockwise to the highest setting.

LINE LEVEL To use FM3 Out 2 for Line Level applications — such as when connecting to FRFR guitar speakers, studio monitors, mixers, etc., confirm the following settings in the Output 2 Configuration section under SETUP > I/O > AudiO:

i: Output Type: Line Level
Output Level: -10dBV or +4dBu (most pro devices operate at +4)

Output 2 Copy: As desired: None, or Out 1 if you want Out 2 to reproduce the signal at Out 1 without needing an OUT2 grid block. You could use this, for example, when connecting to personal monitors via Out 2 while Out 1 is connected to a house PA. Remember though that placing an OUT 2 block on the grid will override the COPY OUT 2 setting, passing instead whatever audio is sent to the grid…
Set Out 2 Mode and Phase as desired.

setup.x: For Line Level applications, set the Out 2 top panel knob as desired, starting fully counterclockwise and then increasing gradually until the desired output level is achieved.

setup.x: A backup of the system settings, created with Fractal-Bot , contains all settings in SETUP.

If you turn off power too quickly after having adjusted entries in the global menus, it may interrupt the autosave process. If that happens, the device will automatically reset the system parameters the next time it's powered on.

i: This means a failsafe was encountered. If the setup data checksum fails, which can happen if the power is interrupted while modifying it, the unit will detect that and revert to default values.

setup.x: If adjusted parameters in the I/O menu are restored to their default values after powering off and on, there’s probably an issue with the internal battery (if the device has one) such as it is exhausted or is loose.

i: Axe-Fx III: The Axe-Fx III uses a battery for system data backup. Whenever the user changes any global data that data is flushed to battery-backed storage. We use battery-backed SRAM instead of EEPROM or FLASH because it's very fast and unlimited endurance. EEPROM is very slow and there's a risk that the user turns the power off before the flush is finished. FLASH has limited endurance (as well as being slower the SRAM) and there's a risk of wear-out. The battery should last 10 years under normal conditions and is user replaceable.
FM3: The FM-3 doesn't have a battery. It uses EEPROM for system data.

factory.x: The current factory presets can be downloaded from Fractal Audio's Support and the user forum .
When you extract the archive file, multiple files are available from that particular factory-presets release date, identified by their bank and associated release. Here's an example for the FM3:
There are three bank files, as well as an ALLBANKS file that contains the three separate banks. For the VP4 and AM4 there's only one bank file.

You can send, AKA "upload", the individual bank files to the device using Fractal-Bot, either the standalone version or the one embedded in your Edit application. You can choose which bank to write the file being stored into on the device; Storing the file to a bank on the device will overwrite any pre-existing presets in that bank.
Storing the ALLBANKS file will ALWAYS overwrite the first 384 presets on the device.
A Presets Update Guide is also included in the archive containing the bank files.
You can restore a single factory preset to the device, without having to restore an entire bank.
For this, use the Import Preset function in Edit. Select a bank file on disk and select the preset you want to restore.

Alternatively, use Manage Presets in Edit to see all presets in a bank file that's stored on disk. In the left browser pane, drag or browse the bank file and let the browser scan it. Pick the preset you want to restore and drag it to the destination slot. You can select a single or multiple presets to drag to destination slots.

After having restored a preset, save it, and then refresh the list of presets in Edit's Preset Picker or Manage Presets window. Clicking the Refresh Button ( ) is a convenient way of refreshing the list.
For more information see the Fractal Audio Knowledge Base article: Installing Factory Presets .

i: If you're not the first owner of the device, start by reading and following the steps in How to reset Axe-Fx III, FM9, or FM3 to a "factory fresh" condition .

factory.x: The previous owner could have modified, moved, or deleted factory presets, which can change your perception of how the presets and the modeler actually sounds. Ensuring the unit is in a factory fresh state is the first step toward your best experience.

i: The presets are configured for FRFR output devices such as studio monitors, headphones, etc., with Amp Modeling and Cab Modeling enabled in SETUP, and using the instrument input on the device.
The VP4 factory presets are split in banks, dedicated to different configurations and instruments: PRE, POST, Bass/Acoustic, 4CM.
The factory presets use Input 1 (instrument) and Output 1 with amplifier and speaker cabinet modeling and are configured for stereo output.

You can use an expression pedal in presets which use External Controller 1; For instance, the majority of presets in the first bank of the factory presets use External Controller 1 for the Wah, however some also add the Vol/Pan or other blocks on External Controller 2 or on other pedal inputs. To figure out which of the various ports are used, navigate in the Edit application for your modeler to…

factory.x: Note: Failing to set the expression pedal correctly can radically change the sound of the factory presets. It's worth taking the time to make sure this is configured correctly.

i: If possible, play the presets in stereo, with the volume turned up, to hear the presets at their best. If you're running mono, and audio output in SETUP is set to Sum L+R , phase cancellation may occur. When using output mode Copy L>R in SETUP, you'll lose the part of the signal that's hardwired to the right channel. That might be a Ping Pong delay or a stereo Cab block with both sides…
For easier control, use the editor.

Preset output levels can vary from preset to preset, though a great effort is made to minimize this. If a factory preset makes the Out 1 Clip LED blink, the overall signal level in the digital domain is too hot. To solve this, turn down Level in the Amp block or in the Global EQ.
If you're wondering why an amp model in a factory preset doesn't sound exactly the same as your own amplifier, read Why Your Amp Doesn't Sound Like Our Amp .
Just like real amps, presets are sensitive to the type of guitar and its pickups.
If you think you've encountered an issue with a factory preset, report it as a possible bug on the user forum .
The presets were dialed in loud so as to be sure the Fletcher-Munson effect did not influence the sound.
I use and prefer low output pickups and the presets work fine for me. I just consider them a starting point as everyone should.

(Cygnus v16) I tested every preset on three guitars this time around: 1) Anderson HSS, 2) American Deluxe Strat SSS 3) Kiesel Vader long scale HH (BareKnuckle). Multiple beta testers also went through the set, and Cliff reviewed Bank A.

Uni-vibe and rotary effects. Amp: Double Verb. Previously: "VIBE AND ROTARY"
EKKOPLEK JUNIORS / EKKOPLEK JRS FM9 / CHRONOECHO FM3

Sound of a vintage Echoplex tape delay with wow and flutter. Some scenes use two amps to maintain the stereo image. Synth produces background noise. External Controller 1 controls tape speed. Amp(s): Jr Blues. FM3: different version
Sharply cut-off reverb. Amp: Matchbox D-30. Use the Performance Page
Multiband compression with Tube Screamer and Octavia drive models. Amp: Plexi. Tip: try the other amp channels

Axe-Fx and FM9:: Crossover splits the signal at a frequency point, after which the two signals are processed separately. Amp: 1987X. Previously: "PLEXI BIAMP". FM3: multiple filter blocks emphasise a fuzzed signal in different areas of the spectrum
DIVIDED BY BURGS / DIVIDED BY BURGS FM3
Divided by 13 CJ11 amp model, dialed in by Burgs (Brett Kingman). Plex Verb, Nobels drive, Fuzz Face, Classic Vibe, Panned delay, Rotary engaged through External 1. PREVIOUSLY: "SWEEP RESONATOR"
Synthesizer, heavy down-shifted notes, and arpeggiator create dark atmosphere. Play single notes. Satans Hollow refers to an old arcade game. FM3: lite version. Amp: Brit JVM
Psychedelic reversed guitar sound through various effects. Amp: USA Pre.
4 delay lines through a stereo panner. Amp: Matchbox Chieftain. External 1: pan rate.
SPRINGS IN CAVES / SPRING IN A CAVE FM3
Features the spring and cave reverb. FM3: single spring Reverb block. Amp: Nuclear-Tone. Previously: "CAVERNOUS".

Produces the sound effect often used in old television series to indicate a dream sequence (4 delay lines which gradually shift upwards in pitch, going through a rotary speaker and stereo panner). Includes the former factory preset "FLASHBACK", which produces the sound effect in old television…

Produces the sound of the Micmix DynaFlanger , a stereo flanging effect often used by Frank Zappa and Dweezil Zappa, going through two amp blocks (FM3: n/a). The flanger is being controlled by an envelope follower. Including the sound from the tv series "Magnum PI". Amps: Brit 800 and Brit JM45.
Stereo tape algorithm in the Delay block, with increasing tape degradation per scene. Amp: Band-Commander.

Various arpeggios using 4 pitched voices in stereo from the Pitch block (placed between amplifier and cab) and other effects. Play single notes. Change key on the Performance page. Amp: Porta-Bass. Includes the former "LAZY MAN'S ARP" preset.
LFO-controlled Wah with detuned stereo delay repeats. Similar to: "NO QUARTER". Amp: 59 Bassguy.
Shimmering reverb, with delay repeats being shifted up in pitch and going through reverb. Amp: Band-Commander.

Tremolo comes after the reverb, with a different type of waveform per scene. The tremolo rate slows down gradually because it's being controlled by an envelope follower. Amp: Class-A 30W. Previously: "TREMVERB".
Touch Wah. The "A3" scene produces the sound of the Korg A3, used in U2's Mysterious Ways . Amp: Supremo Trem.
4 pitch voices from the Pitch block placed between amplifier and cab, create chords in the key of C major / A minor. Play single notes or power chords. Amp: Dirty Shirley.
S(ample) and H(old) filter effect as in Frank Zappa's "Ship Ahoy" , and similar to the Zvex Seek Wah pedal. ACB. An LFO controls a filter. Amp: Brit JM45.
Delay repeats go through a tremolo. The title refers to a Blues Brothers song . Amp: USA Pre.

Funky stuff from a combination of envelope filter and ring modulator. A Scene Controller switches the frequency of the ring modulator per scene. An added 5th in scene 5 gets into synth territory. In scene 6 External Controller 1 controls a delay. Scene 8 "Faux Bass" simulates a bass guitar. Play…
Swampy guitar sound as in ZZ Top's "I'm Bad, I'm Nationwide" . Deluxe Tweed with Tube Screamer.

Crystals effects from the Pitch block and pitch detuning from the Plex Delay block create an atmospheric intermezzo. Scene controllers gradually change the mix of the two Phaser blocks. Play slowly. Amp: CAE3+.
A complex preset that uses a lot of internal controllers and External Controller 1 to create layers of sound. Play slowly. FM3 and FM9: lite versions.

Automatic volume swells, Multitap Delay diffusor, crystals effect, "cavern" reverb, and modulation effects, create blooming stereo sci-fi soundscapes. External Controller 1 controls frequency in some scenes. Play slowly. The preset title possibly refers to the game Final Fantasy. FM3 and FM9: lite…
4 modulated delay lines create rhythm patterns. Amp: AC-20.
Shimmer effect, through pitch detuning, crystals effect and reverb. Play slowly. Amp: Vibrato Verb.
Different types of chorus effects: Tri-Chorus, Dimension-C, dual chorus, 8-voice chorus, quad chorus. Amp: USA Pre.
"ADRENALFLANGE" has a sequencer-controlled flanger, probably based on an Adrenalinn. Amp: Double Verb.
Ring Modulator in tracking mode, adjusted per scene through a scene controller. Play single notes. Amp: ODS-100.
The characteristic through-zero flanged guitar sound from the songs "Starship Trooper" and "W.U.R.M" by Yes]. No cab block. Amp: USA Pre.

LFO-controlled delay voices from Plex Delay blocks through a tremolo, with the tremolo's depth being controlled by an envelope follower. PI Fuzz. The preset title possibly refers to an Eventide effect . FM3 and FM9: single Plex Delay. Amp: Vibrato Verb.
Automatic volume swells go into a delay and gradually drop or rise in pitch. Similar to: "DETUNED DESCENT". Amp: Double Verb. Title refers to an episode of Seinfeld.
LFO makes tape delay repeats wobbly. Reverb into delay creates a stacked "freeze" effect in scene 3. Amp: Vibrato Verb.
Slapback echo in front of a clean amplifier with a spring reverb in Stray Cats style , with tremolo. Amp: Double Verb.

Sci-fi sound waves from 4 delay blocks in series: Delay, Multitap Delay (Diffusor mode), Megatap Delay (rhythmic pattern), Plex Delay (detuned and reverse repeats). Automatic volume swells. Amp: Band-Commander.
Ambient delay pattern from the Plex Delay deliberately forced out-of-tune with a Chorus block, with LFO-controlled stereo panning. Amp: Deluxe Verb.
Long-sustaining stereo delay patterns from the Megatap Delay and Plex Delay blocks create ambience. The Pitch block in scene 3 reacts to the playing (envelope follower). Play slowly. Amp: Plexi.
Four delays from the Plex Delay block into LFO-controlled Wah blocks, panned by the Tremolo/Panner block, followed by compression and chorus. Amp: Deluxe Verb.
Based on Led Zeppelin's "No Quarter" . Wah is synced to an LFO. Similar to the "FRENETICA" preset. Amp: Hipower.
Flanger blocks before and after the amplifier. Amp: USA Rhythm 2.
Spring reverb + bias tremolo = surf sound. Amp: Vibrato Lux.
Hard-knee tremolo is being controlled by an LFO, simulating the use of a "kill switch" on a guitar. Adjust the LFO to change the speed. FAS Modern.
Another preset based on a song by Eric Johnson . Flanging from two flangers (pre and post). Amp: Plexi.
Delay repeats get panned left and right by an LFO, combined with pitch detuning. Amp: Double Verb.
Processed Plexi sound with effects such as pitch detuning, chorus, multiband compression, stereo enhancer, and EQ.

Features two "boutique" amplifiers in a dual-amp setup: Dumble (ODS-100) and Trainwreck Rocket (Wrecker Rocket), with slapback delay. Klone. The FM3 has a single amp block and features the two amp models through scenes.
Ring modulator, low octave, filter, multiband compression, and LFO-controlled frequencies. External Controller 1: more echo. Originally created as a bass line for a reggae song. Amp: Solo 100.
The Edge's (U2) trademark guitar sound, as heard in "Where The Street Have No Name" and many other songs. Amp: Class-A 30W. SDD Preamp, FET Preamp. Preset by Edosounds.
A lead guitar tone, using dual delay. CC Boost. Amp input boost. FAS Lead.

A soothing guitar sound, using drive, delay, tremolo, spring/cavern reverb, chorus, rotary, dual compressors. The Volume block is tied to a scene controller to smoothen scene changes. Amp: Deluxe Verb.
CRUNCHY EVEN IN MILK / TIM'S HOOK 6V6 [FM3]

Dual amp blocks: Plexi 50W and USA MKIV, with pitch detuning. Previously: "STAYS CRUNCHY". FM3: features the Hook Captain 34 amplifier, with some drive and modulation effects (preset by forum member Hippietim).
ARPEGGIATOR M@DNESS (B MIN) / ARPEGGIATOR M@DNESS FM9/FM3

Psychadelic pitch arpeggio through a phaser, sounding like early Pink Floyd. Make sure to try all scenes. The arpeggiator engages through an envelope follower. The sound gets chopped by a sequenced Volume block. Play single notes in B minor. Change key on Perform page. Slightly similar to preset…
Dual amp blocks: Class-A 30W and Class-A 15W, with FET Boost and various effects. FM3: showcases several Class-A amp models through a single amp block.
Clean amp tone, spring reverb, and bias tremolo create the sound of the surf guitar in the James Bond movies theme . Amp: Double Verb, 5F1 Tweed.

Eight synth sounds on the Axe-Fx, with help from LFO and ADSR controllers, including Zamfir pan flute, Moog Taurus bass pedal synth (intro from Tom Sawyer by Rush), ELP-like lead synth, high sine notes, 303 bass synth. Play single notes. External 1 in scene 4. Previously: "ZAMFIR". FM3 and FM9:…
Marshall SV20H Studio Vintage 20. Sonic Drive.
Characteristic mid-heavy guitar sound from Boston . The Axe-Fx preset used a Tone Match block and two amp Brit 800 models, the FM9 and FM3 presets use a single amp block with EQ. Here's a demo
Massive reverb and LFO-controlled stereo rhythmic patterns. Sounds similar to "band delay" presets. Tone of Kings. Amp: Band-Commander.
Envelope-controlled Phaser block, with different sounds per channel, including a talk box simulation. Micro Pitch. Stereo enhancer. Amp: Mesa Pre. Previously: "ENVELOPE PHASER".
Ambient sounds using 8 delays from the Plex Delay. The scenes feature heavily diffused delay lines, detuned delays, pitch-shifted delays (shimmer effect) and crystals. Amp: ODS-100.
Compressed '80s clean sound, with phaser (controlled through External Controller 1). SPX scene. Amp: Double Verb. Previously: "CLEAN POP RHYTHM".
An LFO shifts the pitch of each note, creating an arpeggio. Other scenes add synced delay and flanging. Previously: "PITCHMOD TREM". Plexi.

Stereo tape delay from a Multitap Delay block, with motor speed (including pitch) controlled by External Controller 1, generating sci-fi sounds, with automatic volume swells and various effects. Amp: Nuclear-Tone.
Sci-fi sounds from an LFO-controlled Wah, pitch-shifted delay repeats, and "Cavern"nreverb. The preset title refers to the movie "Logan's Run" . Amp: Vibrato Verb.
Combinations of a lower or upper octave or added 7th from the Pitch block, placed between amp and cab. Amp: Class-A 15W. Fat Rat. Previously: "ORIENT EXPRESS".

Simulated tape distortion, after the amplifier and cab. Two drive blocks are used to maintain the stereo field from the reverb. Amp: Double Verb. Previously: "TAPE DISTORTION". The Axe-Fx and FM9 use three drives, the FM3 two.

Automatic volume swells (adjust ADSR if necessary) with added harmonies from the Pitch block channels (placed between the amplifier and cab). Engage the phaser for more fun. Amp: Vibrato Verb. Previously: "ATMOSPHERE".

The Virtual Capo (dropped tuning) and tremolo recreate the sound and atmosphere of the intro theme of the Twin Peaks television series . "Bari" means "baritone guitar". Play single notes. Amp: Vibrato Lux.

Stereo pitch harmonies through two amp blocks (FM3: single amp). The harmonies shift per scene through a scene controller which is attached to the Key parameter in the Pitch block. Play single notes. FAS Lead.
FREMEN'S SUPER VERB CLEAN / FREMEN'S SUPER VERB FM9/FM3

Contribution by preset designer Fremen. This preset features his take on the Super Verb (Fender Super Reverb) amp model. The FM3 and FM9 presets do not have the 2nd Plex Delay block. Fremen demonstrates the sounds in this video.

Down-shifted, modulated and reverberated crystals and LFO-controlled panning create a haunted house atmosphere. External Controller 1 controls frequencies. Play slowly. Previously: "HORROR MOVIE". FM3 and FM9: single Pitch block.

Mono tape delay, made stereo through two amp blocks on Axe-Fx and FM9. Motor speed is controlled by LFOs. External Controller 1 controls volume (when Volume 1 is engaged). Amp: Vibrato Verb. DELAYSCAPES M@ on the FM3 features complex pulsating stereo delays, using a feedback loop and LFOs.

LFO-controlled synthesizer, made smoother by a RAT distortion and compressor, with a gate to suppress noise. Scenes add a sub-octave and pitch detuning. Play single notes, roll down the tone knob on your guitar to decrease artifacts.
4 pitched voices from the Pitch block plus the original make 5. FAS Lead.

Arpeggio from two Pitch blocks, with stereo panning and more. ADSR controls the arpeggio. Play single notes in C major and let them ring out. Amp: USA Clean. FM3 and FM9: single Pitch block. Engage the Looper block in scene 1 or 2, record a loop, then switch to scene 3 to solo over it.
Based on the Boss BF flanger and Purple Rain by Prince . Amp: 65 Bassguy. Previously: "FLANGETASTIC". Two amp blocks in the Axe-Fx and FM9 presets, one in the FM3 version.
Demonstrates how channel strip preamps (Cab block's preamp simulation) can clip the signal. Amp: Double Verb.
Clean tone with tremolo and spring reverb, with simulated wind blowing in the background. Amp: Texas Star. Previously: "DESERT BREEZE". FM3: single reverb.
External Controller 1 controls stereo panning and flanging. Amp: Brit Silver. FM3: alternative preset.
Sci-fi effects from pitch-shifted delays going through an envelope-controlled filter. Amp: Band-Commander. Play single notes. Previously named: "CAPRICORN 1". FM3: lite version.
HAM & CHEEZ / HAM & CHEEZ FM9 / HAM & FM3

Produces the sound of of a Hammond organ with different virtual drawbar positions. Includes the sound of a Farfisa organ. The rotary rate is controlled through an envelope. FM3 and FM9: lite versions. Amp: JR Blues.
Three ADSR-controlled filters create a synth sound from the 80s/90s. Amp: Deluxe Verb.
Compressor after reverb. 2nd compressor adds more squash. Vibrato Verb.

Various rates of automatic volume swells through the Volume block, with copious amounts of stereo delay and reverb. In one scene, External Controller 1 (pedal) controls the volume. Play slowly. USA Pre. The Axe-Fx and FM9 presets have two Reverb blocks, the FM3 has one.
RAJA DRONE III / RAJA DRONE FM9/FM3

Produces the sound of a sitar with a drone note, through ADSR-controlled filters, pitch shifting, and resonator blocks. Adjust the ADSR threshold for your guitar. FM3 and FM9: lite versions. USA MK IV.

Heavily compressed DI tone ("direct inject": guitar straight into the mixing console). No Cabinet block. Processing includes EQ, slapback delay, stereo enhancer, and stereo pitch detuning. Includes a "Billy Jean" scene, based on the funky guitar part in that song. USA Rhythm 1.

Hit a single note and hear an orchestra, with the help of the synth, pitch shifting, filters etc., and a load of internal controllers. Adjust your attack. External Controller 1 adds arpeggios. Includes a "Strangest Things" scene (television series). The FM3 and FM9 "FM303" preset produces the sound…

Robotic sci-fi sounds from a ring modulator and LFO-controlled synth. The preset title refers to Cylons speaking in the 70's TV show Battlestar Galactica . External Controller 1 is a Whammy in some scenes. Play single notes. Angle Severe.
Bright and compressed Vox AC15 tone (Class-A 15W).
The Multidelay is used to create a ping pong delay that alternates between left-right and right-left, with a different rhythmic pattern per scene. Amp: Vibrato Lux.
Highlights the Rotary block. Scene controllers set the rate per scene for gradual ramping. Class-A 30W.
NEW PLANETS / NEW PLANETS FM9 / THE PLANETS FM3

Pitch-shifted stereo delay repeats create arpeggios, into a "space" reverb and chorus. Play single notes slowly. Set the key in the Pitch block. Similar to the "MYSTIC ARPS" preset. FM3 and FM9: single Pitch block. USA MK IV.
HOME WORLD / HOME SYSTEM [FM9] / HOME WORLD FM3

Space atmosphere from 100% wet diffusors with LFO-controlled time and envelope-controlled feedback, with a phaser, "deep space" reverb, fuzz. External Controller 1 adds effects in some scenes. Includes the former preset "SPACE VERB". The title refers to the game HomeWorld . FM3 and FM9: lite…
Chopped pitch-shifted stereo delay repeats with different waveforms per scene. AC-20.
Sample and hold filters fade in on the tail of ADSR sweeps, using dual-source modifiers, creating a synth-like effect. Hipower.
Stereo delay repeats go down in pitch, using an LFO-controlled Pitch block. Similar "SERENITY NOW!". Includes former factory preset "DETUNED DESCENT". Mr Z MZ-38.
Based on the chorused guitar in "Song for Katie" by Larry Carlton . Different types of chorus per scene. ODS-100.
Plexi amplifier and micro pitch. Different detuning settings per scene.
Eery shimmer effect created by automatic volume swells and shifting detuned delay trails from a filtered Plex Delay. Play single notes slowly. Brit 800.
BAD BY EDO / BAD BY EDO FM3

The Edge's trademark guitar sound, as heard in "Bad" and other U2 songs, using modulated 1/8 dotted delay(s), a Vox and SDD preamp. Use External Controller 1 to fade in the shimmer sound. The Axe-Fx and FM9 presets use dual amps: Class-A 30W and Deluxe Tweed (FM3: n/a). Preset by Edosounds.
Possibly based on a Rocktron Intellifex, a famous effects unit with 8 chorus voices. Demo by Leon Todd . The effect mix changes per scene. Shiver Clean.
Dual clean amps (USA Rhythm 1 and Double Verb). The FM3 preset uses amp channels and has different scenes.
Similar to "S/HIP AHOY": a wah controlled by a sequencer or LFO. Includes the former preset "RANDOM WAH". CA OD-2.
Synth-like sounds using ADSR-controlled filters, flanger, and two Amp blocks on Axe-Fx and FM9. External Controller 1 adds vibrato. Class-A 30W. FM3: lite version.
Country-oriented guitar sounds, using two Amp blocks (FM3: n/a), compression, and tremolo. Mr Z MZ-38. FM9 version has less IRs.
Delay feedback loop, using External Controller 1 for feedback (oscillation) and LFO for wow and flutter, dual amp blocks, and modulation effects. Class-A 30W. FM3: single amp and scene controllers.
Demonstration of low-latency dropped tuning, using the Virtual Capo mode in the Pitch block. Recto.
Tape echo before and after the amp. External Controller 1 controls the tape motor speed. USA Pre.
80's compressed and modulated guitar sound, based on "One Thing Leads To Another" by The Fixx . Double Verb.
Axe-Fx and FM9: dual high-gain amp models panned left and right (FM3: n/a). Amps: Energyball and Recto. FM9 and FM3 presets have less IRs (no 57) and sound darker.
The characteristic chorused and compressed studio clean guitar sound from the 80s. With Tri-Chorus and no cabinet. Various voicing. Class-A 15W. Previously named: "TRI-CHORUS". FM3: light version.
'63 TUBE SPRING VERB / '63 TUBE SPRING VERB FM3
The vintage sound of a '63 tube-driven spring reverb, with various effects. Deluxe Tweed.
Yngwie Malmsteen's signature sound. Plexi 50W. The preset was created by Frank Steffen Mueller.
Rhythmic stereo pattern from the Ten-Tap Delay block, with various effects. Super Verb. In scene 3 of the FM3 preset, TenTap is set to a wrong channel.
RUN LIKE HECK / RUN LIKE HECK FM [FM9] / RUN LIKE HECK FM3

Based on the pulsating modulated stereo delay effect in Pink Floyd's "Run Like Hell" . Hipower. The FM3 and FM9 presets are trimmed down, and the Axe-Fx preset has a Synth scene. Preset by Fremen. Use with a Telecaster.

Recreation of Jimi Hendrix's spaced-out guitar sound, with reversed delay, univibe, Octavia, plate reverb, and LFO-controlled stereo panning and flanging. External Controller 1 shuts down the delay when engaged. Plexi. Previously named: "BASS ACKWARDS".

Ambient crystals effects from the Pitch block into shifted and detuned stereo delays from the Plex Delay block and into an envelope-controlled filter. Input Gain in the second Pitch block is tied to the envelope, to fade in the effect. External Controller 1 adds a voice and "holds" the sound in a…
Rotary speaker into tape delay. External Controller 1 sets the tape motor speed. Class-A 30W. Previously named: "ROTARY BAND DELAY". Tapeverb block created by Simeon.
FLY BY NIGHT / FLY BY NIGHT FM3
Based on the guitar sounds in "Fly By Night" by Rush . Dual amps: Vibrato Lux and Brit Silver. FM3: single amp. Also try Amp 1, channel B.
Ported from the VP4, this presets simulates natural sustain and musical feedback, using ADSR, External 1, pitch shifting and compressors. FAS Lead. FM3 and FM9: slightly trimmed down versions.

Loosely evocative of Jeff Beck (guitar) and Jan Hammer (synthesizer) jamming in the era of the album “Wired” . Includes a recreation of Jeff Beck’s Ring Mod tone. External Controller 1 controls the wah or switches between minor and major. Play single notes. Deluxe Tweed, USA Rhythm 1. FM9 and FM9:…

Based on Eddie Van Halen's guitar sound in the Sammy Hagar-era . EVH 5150 "Block Letter" amplifier and his usual effects, including micro pitch (stereo detuning) and EVH phaser. Dropped tuning through the Virtual Capo in one scene (Axe-Fx only). Previously named: "MODERN EDDIE".
Produces the hall reverb from Lexicon's famous PCM 70 digital effects processor. Band-Commander.
Based on the trademark guitar sound of David Gilmour from Pink Floyd, including uni-vibe, delay, whammy (External 1), and fuzzes. Hipower.

A stereo delay effect, similar to other "band delay" presets, going through a tri-chorus, hall reverb, and LFO-controlled filter, with envelope-controlled pitch effects and automatic volume swells. Play slowly. Hipower. FM3 and FM9: lite versions, single Pitch block.
Various plate reverb types. USA Pre. Previously named: "BRIGHT PLATE".
Singing lead tone from a Marshall JTM-45 and Boss SD-1.

8 detuned stereo delay lines from the Plex Delay block create a large hall reverb, with automatic volume swells. Some scenes use External Controller 1 for manual volume swells. Ganymede refers to a moon nearby the planet Jupiter . Band-Commander.
Clean Fender tone, with a lot of delay and reverb and some chorus, based on "Forty Mile Town" by Eric Johnson . Vibrato Verb.
Dual high-gain amp models, with various EQ settings. Energyball and FAS Modern. FM3: single amp (FAS Modern). Similar to presets "FAS Modern", "Thor's Hammer+Saw" and "Beef Supreme".
Crushing high gain from the FAS Modern model, with various effects. Similar to factory presets "FAS MODERN", "CHUGNUTS" and "UNAPOLOGETIC". Definition of Beef Supreme in Urban Dictionary
Fuzzes through two amps (FM3: n/a) and some effects. Dweezil's Bassguy, Brit JM45.
All-round backline guitar preset, with a Deluxe Reverb, 1/8 dotted delay, and a range of common pedalboard effects. Previously named: "DELUXE DOTTED 8TH". FM3: no reverb.
Ambient soundscapes with automatic volume swells and shifted detuned stereo delays from Plex Delays. Play slowly. Band-Commander. FM3 and FM9: single Plex Delay.

Various combinations of heavily gated high-gain amps in the Axe-Fx and FM9 presets: FAS Modern, Recto, Herbie, PVH 6160, Angle Severe, FAS Skull Crusher. Similar to factory presets "FAS MODERN", "BEEF SUPREME" and "UNAPOLOGETIC". The Axe-Fx and FM9 presets include the former preset "THOR's…
Clean tone with compression, delay, reverb, and some chorus, based on the jazzy song "East Wes" by Eric Johnson . Vibrato Verb.
Characteristic clean guitar tone with tremolo, based on "Born on the Bayou" by Creedence Clearwater Revival . Various overdrives. Deluxe Verb.

Prometheus is a figure in Greek mythology and is a name often used for space-related projects. This sci-fi sound features a tremolo and shimmering crystals going through a sweeping wah. Play slowly. Shiver.
Features the Fryette Deliverance 60 amplifier model. The title refers to the actor Ned Beatty, who played in the movie Deliverance .
Delay trails go through a fast rotary speaker and cloud reverbs. USA Pre. The presets also showcase some of the cloud reverbs.
A KIND OF DREAM / A KIND OF DREAM FM9/FM3

Reproduces the synth-only midsection of "Hemispheres" by Rush . Uses synth, pitch, chorus, filtering, delay, internal controllers, scene controllers. Play high single notes. FM3 and FM9: lite version. Brit Pre.
Hard rock sound from the '80s. Brit 800, with Tube Screamer, detuning, chorus, EQ. The name of scene 5 refers to "New Wave Of British Heavy Metal". Brit 800, Big Hair, USA Pre, Brit Super.
Showcases the model of the Mutron phaser. Dual amp blocks (FM3: n/a). External 1 controls the rate in some scenes. 65 Bassguy.
Scene controllers control transitions between the delay settings, then go through tape distortion. A synth adds vintage hiss. 59 Bassguy.
Features the clean channel of the Bogner Shiva amplifier, with copious delay and reverb. A Tube Driver adds overdrive.
Multiple panned " intelligent" pitched voices through separate amp blocks (FM3: n/a), in the style of Iron Maiden and Thin Lizzy. Play in A minor / C major, or change the key. Plexi and Brit 800.
Various panned rhythmic patterns from the Multitap Delay block. Band-Commander.
Based on "Stone In Love" by Journey . Dual amp blocks (FM3: n/a), stereo chorus, and enhancer. Brit 800 and Plexi.

Complex preset that creates noise and lo-fi sounds with the help of synths, filters, EQ and LFOs. Includes a scene based on the intro of "Wish You Were Here" by Pink Floyd . 5F1 Tweed. Use the Perform Page controls. FM3 and FM9: single synth.
An ultra-clean '80s guitar sound, compressed, with stereo pitch detuning. 1987X. Previously named: "80'S CLEAN".

4 stereo delays from the Plex Delay, creating ambience. Scenes add automatic volume swells, sequenced volume, and envelope-controlled filtering. Play slowly. Double Verb. The FM3 preset is the same but is split into two rows.

Generates various kind of noise, using filtering, pitch shifting, ring modulation and bit reduction. Use External Controller 1 to degrade the sound even more. The Axe-Fx and FM9 presets use dual amps, the FM3 has a single one and the chain is split into two rows. Plexi, Brit 800.
STEREO DEATH FUZZ / ST. DEATH FUZZ FM9 / POST AMP FUZZ [FM3]

Axe-Fx: fuzz and distortion mayhem panned left/right, 4 drives, pre and post amp. Added effects: pitch, phaser. The FM9 has two drives and different scenes and sounds. The FM3 preset features the "Hard Fuzz" model and a single amp, while other scenes add a low octave and post-amp phasing. Bassguy,
Automatic volume swells and detuned and shifted delays. The title is a reference to “Pigs in Space” from The Muppet Show. Double Verb.
Two AC-20 amp blocks with modulation.
Ambient modulated soundscapes, using automatic volume swells, Plex Delay for detuned stereo delays, chorus, and high-feedback flanger. Play slowly. ODS-100. External 1: solo volume.
The title refers to Walt Disney’s LP “Thrilling Chilling Sounds of the Haunted House” . Complex preset, using lots of controllers, to create a range of spooky sounds. FM3 and FM9: lite versions.
The trademark guitar sound of David Gilmour from Pink Floyd in the early days. Stereo delay, chorus, and a different drive/fuzz model per scene. Hipower.
MEN IN THE BOX / MEN IN THE BOX FM9 / MEN IN THE BOX FM

Formant blocks produce different types of talkbox effects, for example as heard in the song "Man In The Box" by Alice in Chains . Controlled by an LFO, ADSR, or expression pedal in different scenes. Previously named: "MAN IN THE BOX". Euro Red.
Preset by Leon Todd. Reverb kicks in when not playing (ADSR). Brit JM45, Cameron CCV.

Cinematic soundscapes in stereo, using envelope-controlled Megatap Delay, Plex Delay, and crystals from the Pitch block. External Controller 1 controls the frequencies in the Filter block in a scene. Play slowly. 5F1 Tweed.
Pitch shifting between dual amps and cab (FM3: n/a). Try chords. Vibrato Verb, AC-20.
Pre and post delays. AC-20 (dual blocks on Axe-Fx and FM9, FM3: n/a). External controller 1 controls Master Delay Time.
Based on a preset in the Lexicon PCM 70 processor. The delay trails make a virtual circle. Amp: USA MK IV Lead Mid.
GNOME MAN'S LANDS / GNOME MAN LANDS 28 [FM3/FM9]
Pitch-shifted 100% wet delay trails (no dry), panned left/right by an LFO, with reverb from a Multitap Delay. USA MK IV, Vibrato Verb.

factory.x: These presets were dropped from the 27.03 factory banks or later. You can still retrieve them from earlier factory preset banks. This is not a complete list.

r: 6TH STONE FROM THE SUN 6TH STONE - FM3

The Pitch block between amplifier and cab adds harmonies (7ths, and in some scene octaves), with pitch detuning, reverb, and stereo enhancer. Not clear if the preset title refers to Third Stone From The Sun, a slightly psychedelic song by Jimi Hendrix. Amp: USA Clean. FM3: lite version.
Delay repeats are shifted up in pitch, with different intervals per scene, with the Pitch block placed between amp and cab. Play single notes. Amp: USA Pre.
Stereo pitch-shifting between amp and cab and a tremolo create oriental vibes, with LFO-controlled stereo panning in the Pitch block. Play single notes. Amp: USA Clean.
Fat auto-wah (envelope controls the Wah block). Amp: ODS-100. Previously: "IN A FUNK".
Stereo pitch-shifted delays from the Plex Delay block. LFOs and ADSR make things crazy. Play single notes. Amp: Jazz 120.

The chorus and vibrato sounds of a Boss CE-1 Chorus Ensemble . Like the original, the processed sound is panned mostly to the left and the dry sound to the right, using dual amps (FM3: single), so listen in stereo. Also features the Vibrato mode of the original pedal. Amps: Double Verb.
This is a mesmerizing swirly stereo guitar sound, using 100% wet Rotary blocks, LFO-controlled filters, and delays. External Controller 1 controls the rotary's rate. Amp: 65 Bassguy.
Phased ping pong delay through an LFO filter.
LFO-controlled sound effect dating back to the first generation of Axe-Fx processors.
Percussive comb-filtered delays from a Multitap Delay. Amp: Band-Commander.
LFO-controlled Pitch and Wah blocks and stereo delay create sci-fi sounding delay trails. The preset title refers to Star Trek . Amp: Band-commander.
Various amps and delays, including circular delay. FM3: different scenes.
Pitch-shifted delays. Amp: USA Pre. Previously: "WIND CHIMES". FM3 and FM9: lite versions.
DOUBLE DIFFUSOR MTD DIFFUSOR FX - FM9 CRONOECHO - FM3

Rhythmic pattern from two Multitap Delay blocks in Diffusor mode. ADSR controls filter frequency and phaser rate. Previously: "DIFFUSED PHASER" on the FM9 using a single Multitap Delay. On the FM3 the "CronoEcho" preset demonstrates the Dual Delay type where the combination of "golden" time ratios…
ECHOES FROM GOD GODLY ECHOES - FM3

Eight repeating and diffused delay lines from Plex Delay blocks, and a consecutive delay adds hard-panned delay repeats with a short delay time to the left and with a long delay time to the right. Amp: Double Verb. FM3 and FM9: single Plex Delay.
Ambient sci-fi effect, using 100% wet Megatap Delay into LFO-controlled panned sweeping filters.

External Controller 1 (pedal) fades in sustained musical feedback from the Pitch block, with pre and post-compression and stacked Tube Screamers. Watch out for bursts of non-musical high-frequency feedback. Amp: USA Clean. FM3: different scenes.
FIFTH TRIBE 5TH TRIBE - FM9 and FM3
Delayed pitch-shifted voices. External Controller 1 adds effects from the Plex Delay. Play slowly and hold notes or chords. Amp: CA3+.

Delayed pitch-shifted notes with lots of reverb, stereo enhancer and automatic volume swells. Sounds like an orchestra tuning before a concert. Play single notes slowly. FM3 and FM9: single Pitch block.
Probably based on the guitar sound in a jazz-rock tune by Jeff Beck . Amp: Double Verb, and Tube Driver.
Percussive Indonesian gamelan sounds , using pitch shifting. Adjust the ADSR controller for best results. Play single notes. Amp: 59 Bassguy. Previously: "GAMELAN NIGHT".

Pitch block in Arpeggiator mode, through stereo delay and pitch detuning. The psychedelic arpeggio is a reminder of early Pink Floyd. Change the number of steps or the key in the Pitch block. Slightly similar to preset "ARPEGGIATOR M@DNESS (B Min)". Amp: Double Verb.
Clean tone through a phaser into 4 shifted stereo delays. Play single notes. External Controller 1 shuts down the reversed delays in scene 2. Amp: Band-Commander. FM3 and FM9: lite versions.
100% diffused signal from the Multitap Delay gets reverberated. Amp: Band-Commander.
Four different phaser types and a synced LFO control the phaser and volume for a tremolo effect. Amp: USA Clean. Previously: "PHASER PARADISE".
Ping Pong delay through Tri-Chorus. Amp: 59 Bassguy.

The title refers to the composer Steve Reich , famous for his compositions based on repetition. This preset creates layers of sound through a delay with long feedback. Watch the Tempo LED. External Controller 1 ends the delay feedback. Amp: Shiver.

Stereo crystals effect from the Pitch block. The preset's envelope follower is assigned to the Pitch block's Input Gain, acting as a fade-in control for the crystals. Diffusion blends the separate trails together in some scenes. See also: factory preset "CRYSTAL ECHOES". Amp: USA JP IIC+. Scenes…
Rhythmic pattern from the Ten-Tap Delay block, panned stereo. Amp: Vibrato Lux. Previously named: "DELAY PAN ALPHA".
Based on the heavily modulated spanky clean guitar sound in "Time After Time" by Cindy Lauper . Flanger, pitch detuning, delay, and pre and post amp compression. Amp: Brit JM45.
Eerie sounds from down-pitched and LFO-controlled detuned crystals, reversed delay, stereo enhancer. Amp: Band-Commander. The title refers to the Valentine's Day massacre in 1929 .
